title: Exploded layers
what: Exactly the locked content: the head (The B2B AI Standard · Open for votes), the title, rows 01–05 and row 06 Your part, nothing added. The form adds physical parts only: each row is its own plate with real thickness edges, threading holes, two dash-dot centre lines running through every plate, the dotted floor, and an empty dashed slot that row 06 was lifted out of.
why: An exploded drawing shows how a thing is put together, which is the point of an open, community-built standard: every rule, skill and scenario is a separate piece someone contributed, held on the same lines. Row 06 is the one piece already lifted out of its slot and outlined in orange — the place left for you.
how: Seven CSS 3D plates share one footprint and are separated only in depth (translateZ) inside a rig tilted 44° and turned 6°, with front and side thickness faces, holes and dash-dot lines as 1px hairlines in neutral tokens; orange only on row 06 and its slot ring. On load the plates sit as one compact slab, then peel apart top-down into the exploded stack (ease-out, staggered, about 1.1s) while each row writes in and its text lines draw; the pointer turns the rig a few degrees so the depth shows, and hovering or focusing row 06 lifts it further. Reduced motion shows the exploded stack static; below 700px the plates flatten into a column of cards threaded by one vertical line, with row 06 as a 44px+ link.
